title: Ravnos and the Dreaming
summary: Why Chimerstry matters to the fae.

claims.text: Of all the Kindred, the Ravnos pose the greatest danger to the Kithain and can affect the Dreaming most, though most of them have no idea of it.

Kithain see Chimerstry as the power to make chimera: anything a Ravnos conjures counts as a chimera its maker does not control, and its weapons and creatures can deal chimerical damage to changelings and the enchanted.

Legend says an eshu, beaten in a talecraft contest by the clan’s founder, granted the vampire sight of the Dreaming; the founder learned to shape it and passed on the illusion-craft, but the sight itself was lost to later generations.

title: Malkavians and the fae
summary: The clan closest to the Dreaming.

claims.text: Madness and odd insight bring the Malkavians nearer the Dreaming than any other clan, and their low Banality makes them the easiest Kindred for Kithain to deal with.
Treaties and compacts between the clan and the fae run back centuries or longer, and many Malkavians recognise Kithain as fae even without seeing the fae mien.
Some simply turn up at freeholds to sit and watch the show, or even to socialise, though certain derangements make for poor relations.

title: Garou Gifts and the Dreaming
summary: How some werewolf Gifts touch changelings.

claims.text: Gifts are tuned to the spirit world, but many overlap with the Dreaming.
Spirit Ward, a level four homid Gift, reaches into the Dreaming and keeps out any chimera.
Sense the Unnatural finds changelings at difficulty 9, or 7 if the Kithain is using an Art; an enchanted Garou using Name the Spirit can identify a distinct chimera.

title: Changelings and wraiths
summary: Why the fae shun the Restless Dead.

claims.text: Kithain have less contact with wraiths than with any other supernatural folk, and most avoid them.
Many sidhe dread anything tied to death, since wraiths show that humans may go on after dying while no one knows what becomes of a sidhe who dies.
Commoners tend to treat ghosts as bad luck, and childlings are split, though the ease many young fae feel around wraiths fades with age.

title: Banality of Eight
summary: The mind of a deeply banal changeling.

claims.text: At Banality 8 a changeling has the outlook of a feeble Autumn Person or a Heavy Sleeper, warding off despair through rigid obsession and seeing anyone different as a threat.

Seelie at this stage struggle to leave home and need friends to lead them out of the fog; Unseelie either climb higher in the Shadow Court or break from it, and rogues cut off from the Court spiral into heavy Ravaging.
